q: Our one-parameter Bell-like epsilon-family yields the tight identity 1 - P_cheat = epsilon, whereas the paper's stated bound is only 1 - O(sqrt(epsilon)). Is the sqrt(epsilon) scaling ever saturated by a concrete concealing protocol, or is 1 - epsilon the sharp achievable bound in every direction and the paper's sqrt(epsilon) is just a slack worst-case Fuchs-van-de-Graaf estimate?
basis: The 41-point sweep in report/evidence/tradeoff_curve.csv shows |P_cheat - (1 - eps)| <= 2.2e-16 across the whole family, i.e. the tight Uhlmann identity P_cheat = F = 1 - eps holds pointwise, not merely up to sqrt(eps).
next_steps: Systematically enumerate 2-parameter and 3-parameter epsilon-families (mixed-Bell, entanglement-swapping schemes, non-symmetric Alice registers) and plot 1-P_cheat vs sqrt(eps) on log-log; identify any family where the sqrt(eps) slope actually saturates. If none saturates, formalize the conjecture that the LC bound is loose by a full square-root factor.

q: The paper requires Alice to keep her share of the entangled state fully coherent until reveal (a 'quantum computer'). How does an imperfect Alice-side quantum memory (depolarizing rate p per delay time-step, or T1/T2 decoherence) degrade the cheating success probability P_cheat, and is there a p_crit at which binding is effectively restored on practical time scales?
basis: The replication assumes noiseless Alice-side evolution (Statevector, unitary U_A). This is the operational bottleneck for real QBC-cheating experiments (Kent's relativistic protocols hinge on exactly this assumption failing) but the paper does not quantify how quickly cheating power decays with memory noise.
next_steps: Add a qiskit-aer noise model (depolarizing channel of rate p on each Alice qubit per delay step) to the sweep, recompute P_cheat via density-matrix simulation, and fit P_cheat(p) for small p. Cross-check against Kent's relativistic-BC binding parameters.

q: For the concealing-quality metric on Bob's side, the paper uses fidelity F(rho_B_0, rho_B_1); operationally, Bob's actual distinguishing advantage is the trace distance D(rho_B_0, rho_B_1) = (1/2) ||rho_B_0 - rho_B_1||_1. Which of the two is the 'right' benchmark axis and does the shape of the trade-off curve change qualitatively when we plot P_cheat vs. D instead of vs. 1-F?
basis: Our figure fixes the x-axis to epsilon = 1 - F. The Fuchs-van-de-Graaf inequalities 1 - F <= D <= sqrt(1 - F^2) allow D to differ from 1-F by a full square-root factor, so the visual verdict ('cheating is essentially total') could look very different on the D axis for a Rick-style operational read.
next_steps: Recompute the sweep with x = D and overlay the two axes; identify the family for which the D-vs-F gap is maximal (should be low-purity Bob marginals); repeat the log-log fit and report both slopes.

q: Kent (1999) and D'Ariano-Chiribella-Perinotti later restore secure BC via relativistic constraints (signaling-limit) and multi-round protocols outside the LC 1-way A->B model. Can we build a small Qiskit-simulable relativistic-BC toy (two spacelike-separated Alice-agents, one Bob) and numerically demonstrate that the Lo-Chau unitary attack fails --- and if so, exactly which step of our U_A construction breaks?
basis: The paper explicitly restricts to protocols with 'one-way communications from Alice to Bob' and this restriction is what makes U_A exist. The current replication does not exercise the boundary of that assumption, so the exact failure mode when the assumption is relaxed is not visible.
next_steps: Implement a 2-Alice + 1-Bob toy where the two Alices cannot communicate after commit; try to construct the analog of U_A and identify the exact structural obstruction (e.g. no product-form unitary exists when the AB purification factorizes across the spacelike cut).

q: For our perfect-concealing GHZ-like example Bob's marginal rho_B is maximally mixed, so U_A on Alice is only determined up to a unitary on each Schmidt block --- many valid cheating unitaries exist. Is there a minimum-two-qubit-gate-count U_A for a given Alice register size n, and does its gate count scale polynomially in n (feasible near-term) or exponentially (attack theoretically real but practically ruled out)?
basis: Our SVD-derived U_A is a dense 4x4 unitary; the paper's argument is existence-only. For a laboratory demo of the cheat attack on real hardware, gate-count is decisive, but the paper provides no complexity analysis.
next_steps: For n = 2..8, generate GHZ-like ideal-concealing pairs, extract the optimal U_A, run qiskit.transpile with basis_gates=['cx','u3'] and record 2-qubit gate count vs n; fit slope.
